problem_solved: Alarm design and assessment for process variables affected by incipient (gradually developing) faults, where stationary alarm-performance models mislead.
model: Piecewise time-variant statistical model of the process variable. Narrowest-Over-Threshold change-point segmentation into 'operational zones' (NOZ, rising zone, fault zone, return to normal). Performance indices MAR, FAR and AAD are computed zone-wise/dynamically. Monte Carlo simulation and Tennessee Eastman Process demonstration.

uses_context_aware_model.answer: partly (time-variant model of the fault trajectory, not of operating context)
uses_context_aware_model.quote: This study proposes a time-variant statistical modeling framework to characterize the behavior of process variables affected by incipient faults.

adaptive_threshold.quote: A new alarm system design methodology is introduced, guided by three key performance indices: Missed Alarm Rate (MAR), False Alarm Rate (FAR), and Average Alarm Delay (AAD).
adaptive_threshold.note: The abstract says a design methodology is guided by the indices. It does not say whether the alarm threshold changes across zones or over time.

regime_specific_threshold.note: 'Zone-specific' in the abstract refers to zone-wise modelling and performance assessment. Zone-specific threshold values are not stated in the preprint abstract; the full text was not accessed.

operating_zone_model.answer: yes, but the zones are fault-evolution segments of the monitored variable, not plant operating modes
operating_zone_model.quote: The methodology uses the Narrowest Over Threshold change-point detection technique to segment the process into distinct operational zones, including the Normal Operating Zone (NOZ), Rising Zone (RZ), Fault Zone (FZ), and Return to Normal (RTN).

transport_evaluation_across_units.note: Monte Carlo simulation plus the TEP benchmark; no multi-unit transport is described.

held_out_confirmation.quote: The proposed method is validated through Monte Carlo simulations and demonstrated using the Tennessee Eastman Process benchmark.

false_alarm_delay_joint_evaluation.quote: In particular, the AAD metric reflects realistic delay patterns and avoids the misleading interpretations often associated with stationary models.

overlap_with_our_work: Moderate on the concept: performance indices (FAR, MAR, delay) differ by zone, and stationary/pooled assessment can mislead. This parallels our point that a single pooled nominal FPR hides zone-wise (phase-wise) differences. FAR and AAD are evaluated jointly.
difference_from_our_work: The 'operational zones' are stages of an incipient-fault trajectory (normal, rising, fault, return-to-normal) in a univariate process variable. They are not operating phases of healthy operation such as climb, cruise and descent. The paper does not calibrate detectors to a nominal healthy FPR, does not transfer thresholds across operating regimes, does not evaluate transport across units or engines, and has no frozen held-out confirmation.

verbatim_quotes.quote: Traditional alarm design methods often assume stationary, which limits their ability to reflect the evolving nature of incipient faults.
By employing a piecewise time-variant model, the alarm system’s performance is assessed in a manner that captures local trends and transitions.
The resulting indices are dynamic, offering a more detailed projection of the process variable’s behavior over time.
Results show that the time-variant model provides a more accurate and interpretable representation of process dynamics and alarm behavior than traditional approaches.

problem_solved: Adapting the threshold of any threshold-type classifier or monitoring rule to a covariate Z (context). The conditional alarm/label rate is made to match a reference (ground-truth) conditional law while the overall false-alarm rate is kept.
model: Threshold function c(z) = Psi^-1(1 - pi(z)), estimated with a nonparametric sliding-window (rectangular-kernel) estimator. The paper gives non-asymptotic bounds, CLTs, functional CLTs, uniform confidence bands, tests of a reference or constant threshold, and change-point tests of the threshold function. The illustration uses FICO HELOC credit data with Z = log(loan amount).

uses_context_aware_model.quote: We show how to modify any given threshold-type classifier resp. monitoring rule to achieve representative conditional label prediction by using adapting the threshold to a covariate Z (the context) to distribute sensitivity while maintaining the false alarm rate.
